feedback.problem:
Let $c=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $d=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $d$ onto $c.$

${\text{proj}}_{c}\,d=⟨$  

{{field-1}},

{{field-2}},

{{field-3}}

$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{c}\,d & =\frac{c\cdot d}{c\cdot c}c \\  & =\frac{{c}_{x}{d}_{x}+{c}_{y}{d}_{y}+{c}_{z}{d}_{z}}{{c}_{x}^{2}+{c}_{y}^{2}+{c}_{z}^{2}}c \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot 5+2\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}}c \\  & =-\frac{14}{14}⟨1,-3,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,3,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
